display.title: Episode 473: The Cup of Eliyahu HaNavi (Chol HaMoed Pesach)
display.summary_short: A Chol HaMoed Pesach show: the freedom of body and soul, Shema with a Beis Yaakov class, the story of a poor woman who would not sell her Kos shel Eliyahu, and why we count the Omer.
display.summary_long: Broadcast during Chol HaMoed Pesach 5751. Uncle Yossi explains that leaving Egypt freed our bodies, but our freedom was complete only when we received the Torah 49 days later, and we pray for the final redemption of body and soul. After the Hakochainik march, a third-grade class from Beis Yaakov of Boro Park recites the Shema, and everyone gives tzedakah. Story time opens with our belief in Moshiach and the cup set out for Eliyahu HaNavi at the Seder, then tells of Devorah, whose precious golden Kos shel Eliyahu was a family treasure. When her struggling husband suggests selling it to pay for Pesach, she refuses and trusts in Hashem. She shelters an old beggar from a storm; his gold coin keeps reappearing on her table, and on Seder night he returns and reveals that he is Eliyahu HaNavi. Finally, Uncle Yossi explains Sefiras HaOmer as eager counting toward the giving of the Torah, encourages children to look closely at the Torah during hagbah, and invites them to write in about it.
display.lesson: Honor the mitzvos and trust in Hashem even when times are hard; kindness to a stranger brings blessing. Count the days to Shavuos with excitement for the Torah.

date.note: 'Here we are enjoying Chol HaMoed Pesach' and the Omer count has begun; the Tuesday of Chol HaMoed 5751 was 2 April 1991, one week after episode 472 (Yud-Aleph Nissan).
